title.narrative: Knowledge exchange coastal protection North Java

description.narrative: Indonesian President Prabowo has made coastal protection of North Java a top priority, aiming to finally initiate construction of the long-discussed Giant Sea Wall. The Netherlands, with its renowned water management expertise and longstanding bilateral cooperation with Indonesia under the MoU Water, is well-positioned to contribute, though international competition proves challenging. Dutch experts have already supported Indonesia in its ambition by reviving the gained knowledge developed during the National Capital Integrated Coastal Development Project (NCICD), comprehensive flood risk analyses of the North Java coast, and the development of a “Go Forward – Defend – Restructure” strategy. In addition, two pilot projects in Demak and Cirebon, backed by Invest International and Dutch companies, have been proposed and included in the Bluebook. A new authority, Badan Otoritas Pengalolan Pantura Java, has been established to accelerate integrated coastal management, though its precise role is still being defined.To strengthen Dutch involvement, timely engagement with the right stakeholders is crucial. The Dutch proposition emphasizes an integrated and inclusive approach that balances short-termresults with long-term strategies and incorporates naturebased solutions. Building on extensive experience in Jakarta’s flood management, the Netherlands seeks to position its expertise and businesses in North Java. This assignment therefore engages two key experts to develop a comprehensive presentation outlining the Dutch proposition towards coastal protection, to conduct a comprehensive stakeholder and power mapping, and to participate in engagement sessions. Key deliverables will include a visual slide deck, a stakeholder inventory, outreach through a “roadshow,” regular updates, and at least one webinar for Dutch stakeholders.
